assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert space E with Borel measurable structure; rank zero is an explicit authored extension.
Any actual probability measure μ on E and any positive real η. No moment or input-density assumption.
The exact graph uses globally smooth compactly supported real representatives; these are existential in the graph equivalence, not a supplied closed-gradient or regularity certificate.
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel structure, including rank zero. Let μ be any probability measure on E and η>0. For independent X∼μ and G∼N(0,I), define the actual joint law J of (X,X+√η G) and its second marginal ν=J.snd. There exists one genuine real linear partial gradient operator D₀ from scalar L²(ν) to E-valued L²(ν), with norm-dense domain, closability and a closed graph for its operator closure. For every scalar class u and vector class v in these two actual L² spaces, (u,v) lies in D₀.graph if and only if there exists a globally C∞ compactly supported real function f with u=f ν-almost everywhere and v=∇f ν-almost everywhere. The gradient is the actual inverse-Riesz Fréchet derivative. No finite moment, input density, potential, integrability, normalizer or gradient-domain certificate is supplied. This is authored background for the paper's density/closedness invocation, not its full rough-input B.13 theorem.
